newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher as mood starts to turn.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher as mood starts to turn.

text.p: Argentine bonds bounced back Monday from the doldrums last week, helped by a general lift in Latin American markets but still suffering from high volatility.

"There was a change in mood today," said a trader at a local bank, pointing to the market's rise despite renewed corruption accusations against government officials by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo on Sunday.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.45 to 117.60, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 3/4 to 80-3/8.
Another trader said firmer markets across Latin America helped return some grace to Argentine bonds that suffered most of last week.

But the trader added that volatility was still very high, with mainly inter-bank trading pushing prices higher. Bigger investors were still waiting to see signs of a more fundamental shift in the market trend.
Traders said the prospect of a string of fresh U.S. economic indicators expected this week including the important jobless report on Friday could mean investors will maintain their cautious approach.
According to traders, the favorable pricing of a Brazilian global bond due November 2001 at 265 basis points over treasuries helped change the mood generally in Latin American markets.
In the money markets, call money fell to 6.48 percent from 6.75 percent Friday.
